title: Core industries: Cement
description: Monthly index of cement production, part of the Index of Core Industries compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT). Base 2022-23=100 (from the June 2026 release; weight 4.41 per cent of the new index (it was 5.37 per cent in the old 2011-12 index)). The previous 2011-12=100 series (eight industries, March 2019 to May 2026, discontinued) is kept as separate views and is not chained to the new one. Published provisionally about 20 days after month end. Cement output is a direct monthly proxy for housing and infrastructure construction, and it is seasonal (strong in January-March, weak in the monsoon). Unit note: this is an index (2022-23=100), not million tonnes; it replaces the stalled Cement Production page for current data.
source: PIB / Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT

qna.question: What is this core industry index (cement)?
qna.answer: The Index of Core Industries (ICI) measures physical production volumes in the core industries: coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity and (new in the 2022-23 series) iron ore. This indicator is cement production.^Following the earlier practice, the ICI weights are derived from the weights of the corresponding items of the IIP.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Index levels compare a month with the 2022-23 average (=100). Production is seasonal, so use the year-on-year growth view for momentum, and treat the latest month as provisional.^Cement output is a direct monthly proxy for housing and infrastructure construction, and it is seasonal (strong in January-March, weak in the monsoon). Year-on-year growth is the figure PIB publishes (one decimal).

qna.question: Base year, revisions and caveats
qna.answer: From the June 2026 release the OEA publishes the ICI on base 2022-23=100 and has discontinued the 2011-12 series (its linking factor for the combined index between the two is 1.47). The 2022-23 series differs in coverage: iron ore added, gross steel production, raw coal only. Old and new levels are not comparable, so they are separate views.^Months are provisional at first release and revised in the following month's release. The figures here come from PIB press releases, whose tables carry the last 13 months, so the new-base history on this page starts in June 2025; the OEA back series from April 2023 is hosted on a website with a broken TLS certificate and is not used.

note: History on the 2022-23 base begins June 2025 (13-month tables in PIB releases).
